question: Should byte-triggered preflight compaction persist retry state and wait for max(1 MiB, 10%) growth before retrying the same active transcript?
rationale: The patch is technically sound, but neither current documentation nor existing behavior defines how long an oversized post-compaction successor may remain above the configured byte threshold; that retry window is a session-state product policy.

options.title: Accept the hysteresis policy
options.body: Adopt the persisted active-file, threshold, and size metadata with the max(1 MiB, 10%) growth rule to prevent every-turn compaction loops.

options.title: Tune the retry window
options.body: Keep the persisted guard but choose a different growth rule and update the focused tests before merge.

options.title: Resolve broader compaction policy first
options.body: Pause this PR if maxActiveTranscriptBytes must remain a strict per-turn ceiling or be coordinated with adjacent trigger semantics.

recommendation.title: Accept the hysteresis policy
recommendation.body: Adopt the persisted active-file, threshold, and size metadata with the max(1 MiB, 10%) growth rule to prevent every-turn compaction loops.
